_comment: Occupancy day-shape and occupant density informed by DOE/NREL Commercial Reference Building Models (Deru et al. 2011, NREL/TP-5500-46861, Large Hotel prototype: ~336 ft^2/person, LPD ~1.0 W/ft^2) and ASHRAE 90.1 Table 9.5.1 (Hotel/Motel LPD 0.70 W/ft^2) / ASHRAE 62.1 Table 6-1 (lobby ~30 people/1000 ft^2, sleeping-area analog ~20/1000 ft^2). The exact hour-by-hour occupancy_fraction/asleep_probabilities curves below are this repo's own illustrative interpolation between those reference points, not a literal reproduction of a published Schedule:Compact table -- not survey/metering-calibrated. gain_w_per_m2 (8 W/m^2) uses this same ASHRAE 90.1 Table 9.5.1 Hotel/Motel LPD figure (0.70 W/ft^2 ~ 7.5 W/m^2, rounded), blended with (not replacing) the per-occupant gains -- see core/buem_adapter.py to_buem_profiles(). Uses hourly_occupancy_curve (not fixed_schedule) because a hotel has no single open/close window: near-constant overnight guest presence plus a checkout dip and check-in peak, which a rectangular open/close/peak model can't represent.
description: Mid-size hotel. Near-continuous occupancy (overnight guests) with checkout/check-in day-shape; guests sleep overnight, front-desk/housekeeping staff work daytime shifts.
